old: In 1872 the Ottoman government made Jerusalem an independent district, a mutasarrifate, answering directly to Istanbul instead of to Damascus. It included Jaffa, Hebron, Gaza and Beersheba. Nablus and Acre belonged to the province of Beirut.
new: In 1872 the Ottoman government made Jerusalem a mutasarrifate, a special district answering directly to Istanbul rather than to the province of Syria centred on Damascus. By the 1900s it covered Jaffa, Hebron, Gaza and Beersheba. Nablus and Acre lay in the Vilayet of Beirut, created in 1888.
